title: SDK Onboarding Quickstart Playbook (WIP)
content:
Purpose: capture a pragmatic, low-friction quickstart and companion docs plan for the Redwood Inference SDKs (JS/TS + Python) — targeted at product engineers who want to ship an LLM feature in <1 hour.

Status: working draft — prioritizing minimal friction, clear defaults, and a single-file quickstart for each language. Alpha internal pairing planned before broader dev preview.

Goals
- 0-to-response in <= 10 lines of user code (install, set API key, call).
- Make recommended defaults align with Hosted API but easy to override for Dedicated/Private.
- Include solid examples for streaming, function calling, and embeddings.
- Capture recommended telemetry/events for cost/latency debugging.

Audience
- Primary: product engineers (frontend/backend) building features (chat, code assist, search).
- Secondary: SRE/platform engineers evaluating integration with Dedicated/Private.

Success metrics (post-release)
- 50% of new hosted API signups run quickstart within first session (via telemetry).
- 20% reduction in first-week support tickets related to authentication/config.
- NPS (quickstart) >= 85 from internal early access cohort.

Design principles / constraints- Keep surface area tiny: one high-level import and one main client.- Sensible defaults: streaming enabled for chat, token limits tuned for 1k-2k sequences, safe timeouts.- No magic: explicit opt-in for advanced batching/kv-cache.- Cross-language parity: same method names and concept mapping (client.generate / client.chat / client.embed).

Quickstart: JavaScript / TypeScript (single-file example)
- Install: npm i @redwood/inference-sdk
- Minimal example (node >= 18, fetch enabled):

```js
import Redwood from '@redwood/inference-sdk'

const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })

async function main() {
  const res = await client.chat.create({
    model: 'redwood-chat-1',
    messages: [
      { role: 'system', content: 'You are concise assistant' },
      { role: 'user', content: 'Summarize the tradeoffs of large context windows.' }
    ],
    stream: true // demo streaming; SDK returns async iterator
  })

  for await (const chunk of res.stream()) {
    process.stdout.write(chunk.delta)
  }
}

main().catch(console.error)
```

Notes: the SDK returns an async iterator when stream: true. For browsers, provide a fetch polyfill or use our browser bundle.

Quickstart: Python (single-file)
- Install: pip install redwood-inference-sdk
- Minimal example (sync):

```py
from redwood_inference import Redwood

client = Redwood(api_key=os.environ.get('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))

resp = client.chat.create(
    model='redwood-chat-1',
    messages=[{'role': 'system', 'content': 'You are concise.'}, {'role': 'user', 'content': 'What are tokenization pitfalls?'}],
    stream=False
)
print(resp.choices[0].message['content'])
```

Integration notes (Concise)
- Auth: SDK reads REDWOOD_API_KEY env var by default. Also supports .redwood/config for local dev and cred helpers for Dedicated.
- Auto region routing: client config { region: 'auto' } falls back to user account region; explicit region overrides for compliance.
- Timeouts: default request timeout = 20s; allow override via client options.

Telemetry & debugging hooks (recommended events)
- events: ["dx.quickstart.run", "sdk.generate.request", "sdk.generate.response", "sdk.error", "sdk.latency", "sdk.token_count"]
- Attach minimal context: sdk_version, runtime (node/python), model, region, lat_ms bucket. Do NOT send prompt content by default; only hashed prompt tokens if user opts in.

Docs plan (bite-sized pages)
1) Quickstart (JS + Py single-file) — single page with copy/paste code + expected output.
2) Streaming guide — example consumers (server-sent events, websocket, React suspense).
3) Function calling + structured output — show mapping of function schemas to typed objects in TS and dicts in Python.
4) Migration guide — Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private (auth, region, network).
5) Troubleshooting & SRE runbook — token errors, rate limits, cold-start latency, fallback patterns.

Staging/Release strategy
- Phase 0 (internal alpha): hand-picked internal teams + engineering docs review (2 weeks).
- Phase 1 (dev preview): public npm/pypi alpha; gather telemetry and support feedback (4 weeks).
- Phase 2 (beta): polish docs, examples, CLI helper for onboarding, sample apps (6 weeks).
- Phase 3 (GA): promote to website, include in quickstart templates.

Checklist before dev preview
- [ ] Publish alpha packages to internal registry & pypi test server
- [ ] Ensure SDK ships source maps and readable stack traces
- [ ] Add telemetry events and opt-out flag
- [ ] Create single-file examples for both JS and Python in repo/examples
- [ ] Add tests for streaming APIs and function-calling parity
- [ ] Draft Confluence page with migration steps and security notes

Open questions / tradeoffs
- How opinionated should default model selection be? (keep it as 'redwood-chat-1' for now)
- Should SDK auto-retry on 429s or expose policy only? (recommend: expose policy, enable simple retry but off by default)
- Embedding interface: flattened vectors vs typed object? (prefer plain list of floats + metadata wrapper)
- How much sample data should docs include before requiring PII redaction guidance? (include a short "do not paste secrets" callout)

Unresolved TODOs (owners)
- Ravi: finalize streaming iterator API shape and error propagation model.
- Sofia: write browser-specific quickstart, include CRA/Vite examples.
- Ethan: build minimal sample app (Next.js) showing chat + embeddings + reranker integration.

Implementation notes for eng team (rough)
- Client core: keep tiny surface and delegate transport to a pluggable layer (node-fetch / urllib).
- Provide prebuilt bundles for browsers (UMD + ESM) with a smaller auth shim.
- Use semantic versioning and experimental flag for breaking API changes.
- Add a CLI helper: redwood init quickstart -> generates example .env + single-file script.

Support playbook (first 30 days)
- Monitor telemetry for sdks: quickstart-run rate, errors per 1k runs, avg latency.
- Weekly office hours during dev preview: 1 hour drop-in for early adopters.
- Keep a pinned Slack thread for quick wins/bugs and escalate repeated feedback to eng triage.

Appendix: example CLI flow (proposal)
- Command: npx @redwood/sdk-init or python -m redwood.sdk_init
- Steps: detect runtime -> prompt user to paste API key or open browser to Console -> generate sample file -> print run command.

Notes to self / scribbles
- keep the docs split: Quickstart vs Deep Dives. Quickstart must not assume prior knowledge of LLM ops.
- demo tokens: show cost estimate line under output (approx tokens * price/token) — helpful for PMs.
- minimal network diagrams for Private deployment: show where SDK talks: control plane vs inference endpoint vs metrics exporter.

References / links
- GH issue for telemetry: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/412
- Console feature request: CONFLUENCE-DEVX-221
- Slack thread: #devx-quickstarts

End of draft.

Feedback welcome — add inline comments or drop into #devx-quickstarts; will iterate on specific code shapes after Alpha pairing.
